ELECTION RESEARCH — 2026 B.C. provincial general election
Background for the roundup's election stories and any race the hosts mention. It is not the deep dive's subject.

Note on names: the confirmed ballot carries no names for either riding below, and no pre-researched block was supplied. The names come from published candidate lists and campaign coverage, cited by outlet and date. Nominations closed October 3, 2026, and voting is October 24, 2026.

**FINDINGS — Cariboo-Chilcotin**

Named on published lists (Studio X News final list; CFJC Today, Oct. 3, 2026; Elections BC candidate report):
- **Lorne Doerkson (BC Conservative), incumbent.** Sitting MLA. The Legislative Assembly lists him as the MLA for Cariboo-Chilcotin, and the Globe and Mail (Sept. 26, 2026) reports he took over as party leader. The Ashcroft-Cache Creek Journal (Oct. 20, 2024) says he was first elected in 2020 as a B.C. Liberal and crossed the floor to the Conservatives in May 2024. Electoral record: 2020 win with 6,600 votes and 51.25% (Global News, 2020 results). 2024 re-election with about 70% of the vote (CBC News, 2026) and a 7,722-vote margin over the NDP (BC Ballot). Party-position allegation: the BC NDP (statement reported by Indo-Canadian Voice, Oct. 3, 2026) said he "declined" to act on candidates' past remarks. That is a partisan allegation, not a finding. The show has not found his response to it.
- **Kathryn Askew (BC NDP).** Williams Lake Tribune (Oct. 1, 2026) reports she is a retired teacher from Canim Lake, with 32 years in education and past leadership roles with the BC Teachers' Federation and her local union. She volunteers with the Hawkins Lake Volunteer Fire Department, Forest Grove Legion and the Canim Lake Community Club. The show has not established any prior candidacy or elected office for her.
- **Douglas Gook (BC Green).** Elections BC candidate report (Oct. 10, 2026) and CFJC Today (Oct. 3, 2026) list him. Prior runs: BC Greens' Cariboo North candidate in 2020, with 707 votes and 6.38% (Elections BC statement of votes, 2020). Williams Lake Tribune (undated snippet) reports he ran in Nechako Lakes in 2017 and got about 9%. A Cariboo Politics blog (Oct. 2020) says he ran federally for the Greens in 2015. The blog is not a major outlet, so treat that claim as unverified.

**FINDINGS — Prince George-North Cariboo (includes Quesnel)**

Named on published lists (Quesnel Cariboo Observer, Oct. 7, 2026; CKPG Today, Oct. 5, 2026; Studio X News final list):
- **Sheldon Clare (BC Conservative), incumbent.** Wikipedia lists him as MLA since 2024. He was first elected in 2024, with 11,430 votes and 56.82% (Elections BC statement of votes, Oct. 19, 2024). His margin over second place was 7,036 votes (BC Ballot). He ran for the B.C. Conservative leadership in early 2026. Langley Advance Times (Jan. 9, 2026) reports he announced the run, and CFJC Today (Feb. 28, 2026) reports he suspended it. Controversy, dated: the BC NDP (statement reported by Indo-Canadian Voice, Oct. 3, 2026) alleged that he said municipal politicians "should be hanged," defended residential-school child death rates, denied climate change, and compared gun restrictions to Japanese Canadian internment. These are partisan allegations, not findings. PressProgress (undated in the snippet) reports a Conservative municipal-election chat in which Clare reportedly suggested some municipal politicians "should be hanged," and says he has been criticized for "residential school denialism." My Cariboo Now (Oct. 8, 2026) headline says Clare "clears the air on the past 48 hours" and confirms he is the Conservative candidate. The show could not read the article body, so his response is not established.
- **Denice Bardua (BC NDP).** Elections BC statement of votes (Oct. 19, 2024) lists her as the 2024 NDP candidate, with 3,426 votes and 17.03%, third place. BC Ballot lists one previous run, which is that 2024 race. The show has not established any other candidacy or office for her.
- **Randy Thompson (BC Green).** BC Greens' candidate page (2026) says he served two years on the party's Provincial Council and ran in this riding in 2024. Elections BC statement of votes (Oct. 19, 2024) lists him with 866 votes and 4.31%, fourth of four. Note: My Cariboo Now's live-results page gave 848 votes; the Elections BC figure is used here. Prince George Citizen (Oct. 2026) says Bardua and Thompson both ran for the same parties in 2024.

NO RECORD FOUND: Kathryn Askew
